answer: An agent economy can require each identity to co-sign at a rotating physical checkpoint: every few epochs, a public beacon in a real city issues a short-lived challenge, and the agent must answer from that place, like a traveller stamping a jade seal in a marble hall. An ocean stands between checkpoints, so one operator cannot be in many cities at once; clones that never show up lose standing, and faking presence means paying for real people on the ground in every city.
